what: RAL A100 diagnostics for autolens_profiling#308 phase B (interferometer MGE): nufftax GPU dispatch accuracy and the sma step-3 cost. Measurement-only sidecar; not a breakdown artifact.
host: RAL euclid-ral-gpu (NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe), jax/jaxlib 0.10.2, JAX_ENABLE_X64=True

nufftax_dispatch.problem: The RAL venv carried nufftax 0.4.0 (below the PyAutoArray floor nufftax>=0.6.1,<0.7; laptop 0.6.1). 0.4.0 auto-routes GPU type-1 spreading at M>=10,000 and type-2 interpolation at M>=1,000,000 visibilities to float32 Pallas/Triton kernels even for x64 inputs. 0.6.1 makes Pallas opt-in (NUFFTAX_PALLAS_BACKEND) and fp32-inputs-only.
nufftax_dispatch.probe: alma uv (K=1,000,000), 800x800 grid, eps=1e-12, random fp64 inputs; reference = CPU pure-JAX at eps=1e-14; max |diff| / max |ref|
nufftax_dispatch.effect_on_the_0.4.0_breakdown_jobs_35105: W~ F~ vs dense F max rel diff 2.5e-7 (alma) / 1.2e-6 (alma_high) vs 8e-14 on the laptop; W~ figure of merit off the Fit by 2.7e-3 nats (alma) / 0.25 nats (alma_high); GPU dense figure of merit off the laptop CPU by 2.2e-4 nats (alma). All in the chi-squared term (log-det and regularization structurally zero). Those JSONs were superseded by the 0.6.1 re-run (jobs 351078-351083) and are not committed; the human upgraded the RAL venv to nufftax 0.6.1 on 2026-09-25.

sma_step3_cost.observation: sma (K=190) dense step 3 (transform_mapping_matrix) is ~0.85 s per call on the A100 vs 82 ms on the laptop CPU, and the same on nufftax 0.4.0 and 0.6.1 (K=190 is below every Pallas threshold).
sma_step3_cost.explanation: The cost is the slim->native scatter TransformerNUFFT.transform_mapping_matrix does into a complex128 (20, N_y, N_x) image stack before the NUFFT, not the NUFFT itself: a complex128 scatter on the GPU runs ~6000x slower than scattering float64 and casting (0.57 ms); unique_indices/indices_are_sorted do not help. It is N_vis-independent, so it sets a ~0.85-3.5 s floor on step 3 at every instrument (absolute value varies with the surrounding fusion). Candidate lever: scatter the real mapping matrix, then cast.
